home.title: Use your smart card, USB token, or OS certificate to sign on any website.
home.lead: Works with Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Opera, Brave and Safari on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Free and Open Source for everyone.
home.how1: Prepares the document and sends only its hash, a short fingerprint. The document stays with the site.
home.how2: Passes the request from the browser to the SignLocal app. It never sees your PIN or your keys.
home.how3: Shows who is asking and a verification code. You choose the certificate and confirm.
home.how4: Windows, macOS or the token driver signs the hash. If a PIN is needed, you type it there.
home.how_note: The document never leaves the website. Any signature format, for any country, can be built on top: PAdES, CAdES, XAdES, JAdES.
home.p1_h: Your PIN never passes through the browser
home.p1: The PIN is typed in the app or in the operating system window, never in a web page and never in the extension.
home.p2: A website sees nothing about your certificates until you allow it, and you can revoke that at any time in the app.
home.p3: Even for a website you allowed, each signature opens the app's window with a verification code you can compare with the site.
home.p4: The app receives a fingerprint of the document, not the document. Nothing runs in the background and no network port is opened.
home.compat_note: Status per browser, system and device, including what is still being tested:
home.faq_a1: Yes, for everyone, with no account. The app and the extension are free software (GPL-3.0-or-later); the libraries for developers are Apache-2.0, so any website or program can use them.
home.faq_a2: Any certificate your operating system or your token's driver can use: USB tokens, smart cards and certificates installed on the computer (for example from a .pfx file). There is no list of approved models.
home.faq_a3: No. The PIN is typed in the app or the system window, and the private key never leaves your computer or your token. A website only receives the certificate you choose and the signature you confirm.
home.faq_a4: Prerelease builds are not code-signed yet. The download page says what to click, and how to check each file against the published SHA256SUMS.
home.faq_a5: SignLocal returns a raw signature and the certificate; the website builds the format it needs (PAdES, CAdES, XAdES or JAdES), for any country's rules.
home.faq_a6: No. SignLocal runs on computers with Windows, macOS or Linux, where tokens and smart cards are plugged in.
home.faq_a7: No. The browser starts the app only when a website asks for a signature, and the app opens no network port.
home.faq_q3: Can a website see my PIN, my keys or my other certificates?

home.how_back: The signature and your public certificate go back to the website, which builds the signed document.
home.how_lead: The website never touches your keys. Everything that involves your certificate happens on your computer, in a window you control.
home.how_local: On your computer: the PIN never leaves it
home.mobile: SignLocal runs on computers with Windows, macOS or Linux. Open this page on your computer to install it.
home.unsigned_note: Prerelease builds are not code-signed yet, so Windows and macOS warn once. Every file has a published checksum.
home.works_lead: No list of approved models: if your operating system or your token's driver can use a certificate, SignLocal can sign with it.
dl.title: Download SignLocal
dl.lead: Two parts work together: the app on your computer and the extension in your browser. Install both, then finish the setup.
dl.unsigned_h: Prerelease builds are not code-signed yet
dl.unsigned: Windows shows SmartScreen and macOS shows Gatekeeper the first time. The steps below say what to click. Code signing is planned. Always check the SHA256SUMS file.
dl.private: The repository is private for now, so downloads need the GitHub CLI signed in (gh auth login).
dl.win: The installer script checks the download, installs SignLocal for your user (no administrator rights) and connects it to your browsers.
dl.mac: The installer script checks the download, installs SignLocal.app without sudo and connects it to your browsers.
dl.linux: The installer script works on any distribution and installs for your user, without root. On Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora and Rocky Linux it can install the system package instead.
dl.verify: Each release has a SHA256SUMS file. Compare the hash of your file with its line. The installer scripts do this for you.
dl.guide: Full guide, file names and uninstall steps: docs/install.md
dl.cr_keep: Keep that folder: the browser loads the extension from there.
dl.cr_load: Click Load unpacked and choose the unzipped websign-extension-<v>-chromium folder.
dl.devkey: The unpacked extension carries a public development key, so the app can recognize it before it is in a store. Only load the zip from our release after checking SHA256SUMS, and remove unpacked extensions you do not trust. Every signature still needs your confirmation in the app window.
dl.ext_intro: The extension is not in the stores yet. From the same release, download websign-extension-<v>-chromium.zip (for Firefox: websign-extension-<v>-firefox.zip), check it against SHA256SUMS and unzip it.
dl.ff_keep: A temporary add-on lasts until Firefox restarts. To keep it, use Firefox Developer Edition, Nightly or ESR: set xpinstall.signatures.required to false in about:config, then in about:addons choose Install Add-on From File and pick the zip.
dl.ff_load: Click Load Temporary Add-on and choose manifest.json in the unzipped folder.
dl.ff_open: Open this page and choose This Firefox:
dl.finish: The installer already connected the app to your browsers. Sign a harmless test message to check that everything works. If the extension cannot find the app, open the activation page once.
dl.mac_arch: One app for Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
dl.mac_warn: The app is not notarized yet. If you installed it by hand and macOS says it cannot be opened, open System Settings, Privacy & Security, and click Open Anyway, or run: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/SignLocal.app
dl.mismatch: A mismatch means the file is damaged or was altered: delete it and do not run it.
dl.pcsc: Smart cards and tokens need the PC/SC service:
dl.safari: The Safari extension comes inside SignLocal.app (macOS 13 or later, Safari 17 or later): nothing else to download. Until the app is signed by Apple, Safari loads it only with a developer setting.
dl.sf1: Install the app for macOS above and open SignLocal once from Applications, then close its window.
dl.sf2: In Safari, open Settings, Advanced, and turn on Show features for web developers.
dl.sf3: Open Settings, Developer, and turn on Allow unsigned extensions. Safari asks for your Mac password.
dl.sf4: Open Settings, Extensions, tick SignLocal and allow it on the websites where you sign.
dl.sf_restart: Safari turns Allow unsigned extensions off every time it quits: repeat step 3 after each restart. Certificates in the Keychain and tokens that work with macOS behave as in other browsers; tokens that only have a PKCS#11 driver may not work in Safari yet.
dl.win_warn: If you unzip and run websign.exe by hand, SmartScreen says “Windows protected your PC”: click More info, then Run anyway. The script avoids this prompt.
pv.title: Privacy
pv.lead: SignLocal is built to know as little as possible. There are no trackers on this site and the product needs no account.
pv.t1: Your certificates, your PIN and the keys never leave your computer. The app asks the operating system or the token driver to sign.
pv.t2: Only what you approve: the public certificate you chose and the signature of the hash it sent. Never your PIN or your private key.
pv.t3: A website or program is remembered only if you tick the box. The list is in the app, with a Revoke button.
pv.t4: Diagnostic logs contain no names, ID numbers, serial numbers, digests, PINs or certificate contents. Copying diagnostics is your choice.
pv.t5: It has no cookies, no analytics and no external fonts or scripts. The language you pick is remembered only in your browser.
pv.t6: Questions or reports: open an issue in the source repository.
dev.title: For developers
dev.lead: Let people sign on your website with the certificate they already have. You build the document and its hash; SignLocal returns the signature and the certificate.
dev.install: Install the package. It has no dependencies, is fully typed and adds under 5 KB to your page.
dev.quick: Then sign. prepare receives the certificate the person chose and returns the hash to sign:
dev.quick_note: result.signature is the raw signature (ECDSA r‖s, or the RSA block). Put it in your CMS or PDF together with result.certificate.der and result.certificate.chain.
dev.prepare1: Your page calls sign(). The SignLocal window opens and the person chooses a certificate.
dev.prepare2: prepare(certificate) runs in your page. PAdES and CAdES put the certificate inside the signed data, so this is where you build the signed attributes and return their hash (32, 48 or 64 bytes).
dev.prepare3: The person compares the verification code and confirms, typing the PIN in the app if needed. The document never leaves your page.
dev.prepare4: sign() resolves with the signature. If the person switches certificate, prepare runs again and only the last hash is signed.
dev.types: The types follow your options: with hash: "SHA-384" and algorithm: "ECDSA", prepare's context and the result are typed with exactly those values.
dev.status_h: Show the Sign button only when SignLocal is ready
dev.status: status() never opens a window and never fails. problem says what is missing; onChange tells you when the person installs or updates something while your page is open.
dev.errors: Every failure is a WebSignError with a stable code, a message and a hint for you, and a docsUrl that points to this table. For the person, errorText(error) from @websign/sdk/messages gives a title and the next step in 7 languages.
dev.col_meaning: What happened and what to do
dev.err.ExtensionMissing: The SignLocal extension did not answer: it is not installed, or it is disabled for this site. Show a link to installUrl().
dev.err.AppMissing: The extension is there but the SignLocal app is not. The person installs the app; the extension guides them.
dev.err.AppOutdated: The app is older than the extension needs (details has both versions). The person updates the app.
dev.err.ExtensionOutdated: The extension is older than the app needs. The person restarts the browser so it updates.
dev.err.ClientOutdated: The extension only speaks a newer protocol than your copy of @websign/sdk. Update the package in your site.
dev.err.InsecureOrigin: The page is not served over https. Serve it over https (http://localhost also works).
dev.err.Aborted: Your AbortSignal fired, or prepare threw (your error is in cause). Nothing to show the person.
dev.err.UserCancelled: The person closed the window. Leave the page as it was; no message is needed.
dev.err.Timeout: Nobody confirmed in time, or prepare took more than 60 seconds. Offer to try again.
dev.err.NoCertificates: No usable certificate was found. The person plugs in the token or card and tries again.
dev.err.CertificateUnavailable: The chosen certificate is gone (the token was removed). The person plugs it back in or chooses another one.
dev.err.CertificateNotValid: The certificate has expired or is not valid yet. The person chooses another one.
dev.err.InvalidRequest: A bug in the call: a wrong option, or a hash of the wrong length. The message says which.
dev.err.UnsupportedAlgorithm: The key cannot produce the algorithm you asked for. Accept more algorithms, or ask for another certificate.
dev.err.PinIncorrect: A wrong PIN. The app asks again, so a website rarely sees this.
dev.err.PinLocked: The PIN is blocked. The person unlocks it with the PUK, using the issuer's tools.
dev.err.TokenRemoved: The token was removed while signing. The person plugs it back in and tries again.
dev.err.DriverFailure: The token driver failed; details.native has its status. Try again; if it keeps failing, the person reconnects the token.
dev.err.Busy: Other requests are waiting in the SignLocal window. Try again once they are done.
dev.err.Internal: A bug in SignLocal. Please report it with the diagnostics from the app.
dev.testing: @websign/sdk/testing installs a fake extension and app on window. Your code runs unchanged: status(), certificates() and sign() work, prepare runs, and the signatures are real ECDSA or RSA made with public test keys, so you can verify them. Script every outcome: the person cancels, no certificates, app missing, outdated, driver errors.
dev.testing_dev: The same fake lets you build your page before installing anything. Load it only in development:
dev.testing_warn: Anyone can sign with its keys. It refuses to run outside localhost-like addresses and warns on the console when installed.
dev.frameworks: The SDK has no framework code. The examples include a copy-paste useWebSign() hook for React and the same as a Vue composable: live status, progress, error, and cancelling when the component goes away.
dev.pdf: Your PDF library reserves room for the signature and hashes the rest of the file. In prepare you build the signed attributes for the chosen certificate and return their hash; the signature you get back goes into the CMS inside the PDF. The PAdES example does this with pdf-lib and PKI.js, and its test checks the result with OpenSSL.
dev.api: Every function and type of @websign/sdk, @websign/sdk/messages and @websign/sdk/testing, with examples, generated from the source.
dev.desk: Connect to the app, then call sign(). The app names your program in its confirmation window.
dev.rust: Client::connect(), then certificates() or sign(). The app is started on demand.
dev.docs: API guides and contracts in the repository: docs/architecture/web-api.md and docs/architecture/desktop-api.md
test.title: Test your setup
test.lead: Check that the extension, the app and your certificate work together. It takes one minute and signs only a harmless sample text.
test.local: The sample text, your certificate and the signature stay in this browser and on your computer. This page has no server side and keeps no record.
test.checking: Looking for the extension and the app…
test.ext_missing_h: The browser extension is not installed
test.ext_missing: Install the SignLocal extension for this browser, then check again.
test.app_missing: The extension is there, but the SignLocal app was not found on this computer. Install it and open it once, then check again.
test.outdated: The SignLocal app is older than the extension needs. Install the latest version, then check again.
test.ready: The extension and the app are installed and compatible. Continue with the test below.
test.sign_p: This signs a fixed sample text with your certificate. The app opens its own window: choose a certificate there, confirm and, if asked, type your PIN there. Never in this page.
test.waiting: Waiting for you in the app window…
test.code_hint: Compare it with the code the app showed in its window. If they differ, do not trust this signature.
test.v_verified: Verified in this browser with the certificate's public key.
test.v_invalid: The signature does NOT match the sample text. Something is wrong: copy the result for support.
test.v_unsupported: Signature received, not verified in the browser.
test.support_p: This summary has no name, CPF or certificate data: only algorithm, key type, result and error code.
test.copy_failed: Could not copy. Select the summary above and copy it yourself.
test.nocrypto: This browser cannot run the check (WebCrypto is unavailable). Open the page over https in a current browser.
act.title: Finish setting up SignLocal
act.lead: You installed the app. One more step connects it to your browsers. It takes a few seconds.
act.allow: Your browser asks whether to open SignLocal. Allow it. The app sets itself up for every browser on this computer and opens a short getting-started window.
act.none: The app is probably not installed yet. Install it from the download page, then come back and press the button again.
